justification.text: This is the problem's max_{n<x} d_n d_{n-1} / (max_{n<x} d_n)^2. primeGap n = nth Prime (n+1) - nth Prime n ≥ 1 for every n (consecutive primes are distinct, so no truncation), so for x ≥ 1 the sup over the nonempty range is ≥ 1 and the denominator is positive; it is zero only at x = 0, which cannot affect the limit x → ∞. (The n = 0 term's truncated index gives d_0 d_0 = 1, never above the later terms, so the numerator agrees with the informal max.)

justification.text: At n = 0 the term d_0 · d_(0-1) reads d_0 · d_0, a single fixed value standing in for the undefined d_(-1). Inside a max whose denominator (max d_n)^2 tends to infinity, a fixed term c contributes at most c / (max d_n)^2 → 0, so it cannot change the limit.
